title: Q3 Usage & Resilience Strategy Review - Redwood x Ironbridge
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-03 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~58m | Recording id: ff-20260903-8421
Attendees: Maya (Redwood), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM); Samir (Ironbridge CTO), Lina (Platform Eng), Avery (ML Ops), Jordan (Finance), Tess (Security)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you all squeezing this Q3 check-in in. we'll go 60 minutes, agenda: usage trends, cost drivers, a reliability recap, and then roadmap sync and next steps.
[00:18] Samir: yep, thanks Maya. quick thing Jordan has to jump off sometime at 45, so we'll try to get to pricing and forecast early.
[00:25] Diego: cool, I'll start with the usage overview and then Priya will cover adoption metrics.
[00:35] Diego: So we've seen token volume up about 38% q/q, nice growth. Most of the delta is from the new summarization feature hitting production in mid-July. that feature is heavier on longer generation lengths, so your avg tokens per call moved from ~420 to ~890.
[00:50] Lina: yeah that matches our telemetry. We also rolled the batch processor to 2x concurrency which bumped short-tail latency but improved throughput.
[01:05] Diego: Right, so two levers at play: longer sequences and different batching. we flagged a cost increase in August — that's primarily from the freeform summaries spiking tokens.
[01:20] Jordan: to be blunt, finance flagged the 27% increase in monthly bill, we need a path to flatten that.
[01:28] Maya: understood — we have a few recommendations: prefix caching for repeated intro prompts, and a quantization profile suggestion for your fp16 model variant, Diego will go into perf numbers.
[01:40] Diego: on perf: we ran a dedicated benchmark on your dev cluster last week — when using the 4-bit quant profile we saw token cost drop ~36% with tail-latency increase of ~40–60ms at 99th percentile, and no measurable diffs in our prompt tests. caveat: we need to validate across your longest contexts.
[01:58] Avery: is that safe for our regulated docs? we have PII redaction in the pipeline.
[02:05] Tess: security here — we need to ensure key management integrates with our on-prem HSM — remember Ironbridge needs customer-managed CMKs.
[02:14] Maya: absolutely. Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations, Priya will share the integration runbook after the call.
[02:22] Priya: noted — will attach runbook and a short checklist.
[02:30] [02:30] Samir: let's talk incidents — we had two production degradations in July and Aug, one was scheduler saturation, one was an autoscaler misconfig during a spike.
[02:42] Diego: yep those were root-caused: the first was a burst of prefix-cache misses from a bad rollout that invalidated caches; the second was an aggressive pod termination policy in k8 that didn't respect in-flight KV cache warmups. we've proposed a safer rollout config and a circuit breaker for scale events.
[03:05] Lina: any change to SLOs? we need a formalized bladder for 95/99 targets so we can alerting.
[03:12] Priya: we've put together a suggested SLO: 95th < 220ms, 99th < 650ms for the standard nlp endpoint for your traffic profile. it's a starting point, can be tuned.
[03:25] Samir: can we get per-route SLOs? our embedder route is super latency-sensitive.
[03:31] Diego: yes per-route and per-model SLOs are supported; we'll share a dashboard template.
[03:37] [03:37] Jordan: quick cost question — dedicated vs hosted, is it worth committing? numbers?
[03:43] Maya: great question — for your traffic profile, our rough calc shows Dedicated with committed monthly capacity would lower unit cost by ~22% if sustained, but you'd need a 6–9 month commit to break even vs hosted. we'll send the detailed cost model.
[03:58] Jordan: ok that's helpful.
[04:05] [04:05] Tess: compliance — SOC2 renewal is Q1 for us; will Redwood provide updated audit artifacts and an on-demand audit log export?
[04:14] Priya: yes, security pack and an S3 export hook for audit logs is available, plus quarterly SOC attestations. I'll share the security packet link: https://redwood-hosted.example/security-pack-ironbridge (note: placeholder link).
[04:30] Avery: we also want to run a controlled performance POC to validate quantized variants and steward key rotation impact. can Redwood help?
[04:38] Diego: absolutely — propose a 2-week perf POC: week 1 synthetic workloads + prefix cache tuning, week 2 long-tail tests on your staging datasets. we'll need a small dedicated test pool.
[04:52] Samir: timeline wise, we want results before the procurement review on Sep 30.
[04:57] Maya: doable — we'll aim to kick POC next week.
[05:04] [05:04] Diego: moving to reliability playbook — we recommend: 1) cache warming on deploy, 2) staged rollout with traffic mirroring, 3) conservative pod termination grace to avoid KV loss, and 4) circuit breaker thresholds on queue depth.
[05:20] Lina: how intrusive is cache warming to deploy cadence? our teams prefer frequent deploys.
[05:26] Diego: warming can be parallelized; we can do a lightweight warming pass that doesn't block deploys — just warms hot prefixes.
[05:34] Samir: do you have a prescriptive rollback? last time rollback had a 7-minute flapping window.
[05:41] Diego: yes we'll propose a canary threshold + automatic rollback at X error rate; also we recommend blackbox canary traffic, not full traffic.
[05:49] Priya: ops note — we'll add a runbook card to the Console under 'Ironbridge -> Runbooks' with step-by-step.
[05:57] [05:57] Jordan: financing — can you provide a month-by-month projection with committed vs on-demand so we can model capex vs opex?
[06:05] Maya: yes we'll provide a 12-month forecast spreadsheet with sensitivity bands.
[06:10] Jordan: perfect, thanks.
[06:15] [06:15] Samir: roadmap items — we're curious about Redwood's upcoming model upgrades and regional expansions, esp APAC.
[06:23] Diego: roadmap: public: adding a quant-aware kernel for 8->4 bit conversions in Q4, improved streaming latency optimizations, and APAC region in late Q1 next year. subject to change.
[06:36] Lina: will the APAC region support private deployment? we need VPC peering.
[06:41] Maya: yes private deployments and VPC peering are on the plan for the initial APAC rollouts.
[06:47] [06:47] Tess: can we get an encryption-at-rest detail? our audits require algorithm names and key lifecycles.
[06:54] Priya: will send the security pack with CRYPTO details including AES-GCM 256 and CMK rotation cadence.
[07:00] Avery: on adoption — we've seen across your teams that the teams using prefix templates have 2.7x fewer token costs per session, that seems promising.
[07:12] Diego: yes, templates + deterministic prefixes are the low-hanging fruit. we also recommend a prompt linting pass to reduce repeated assistant verbosity.
[07:22] Samir: what's the impact of KV cache TTLs? we recently shortened them to save mem.
[07:29] Diego: TTL reduction reduces mem but increases token regen costs; recommended hybrid TTL: shorter for cold prefixes, longer for stable session prefixes. we'll share a TTL tuning guide.
[07:40] [07:40] (discussion continues, skipping small back-and-forth)
[09:05] Maya: recap and next steps: agree to kick a 2-week perf POC, we will send security pack and runbook, finance gets a 12-month committed vs on-demand model, and we'll provision a dedicated test pool next week.
[09:20] Jordan: action items for your team: provide staging dataset pointers and access controls for the POC.
[09:30] Samir: one last Q — are you planning any prebuilt evals for summarization quality?
[09:36] Diego: yes we have a summarization eval harness, we'll share curation notes and baseline metrics; we can run it on your staging dataset as part of POC.
[09:45] Priya: I'll schedule a short 30-min kickoff for the POC for next Tue and send calendar invite.
[09:52] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and forecasts by EOD tomorrow, and circle back after POC.
[09:58] End recording.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional word swaps (K-V vs KV), minor punctuation skips, speaker overlaps; overall medium fidelity.
summary: Q3 check-in focused on rising token usage from a new summarization feature, resulting cost increases; two recent production incidents were root-caused to cache invalidation and aggressive autoscaler policies. Agreed to run a 2-week perf POC to validate quantized model profile and prefix-caching; Redwood to provide security pack, runbooks, and 12-month cost forecast. SLO templates and dashboard will be shared; next touchpoints include POC kickoff and forecast delivery.
topics: Cost drivers & committed vs hosted pricing

Redwood - Provision dedicated test pool and kick off 2-week perf POC next week (owner: Diego)
Redwood - Share 12-month committed vs on-demand cost model (owner: Maya)
Ironbridge - Provide staging datasets and access for POC (owner: Samir)
